repo.description:
When a record is deleted, SurrealDB removes the graph edges connected to it. That edge removal is meant to run with the caller's permissions, so an edge table's `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` clause still applies - deleting an endpoint vertex must not let a caller erase edges they could not delete directly. A previous fix (GHSA-whwg-vh4f-pmmf, patched in 3.1.0) established this for a direct vertex delete.

A second route escaped that guarantee. A `DEFINE FIELD ... REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE` deletes the referencing record when the referenced record is deleted, and it computes that cascading delete with permissions disabled - which is deliberate, so referential integrity can complete regardless of what the caller may do to the referencing record. But permission enforcement was a single frame-wide flag, so the disabled state flowed on into the referencing record's own edge cleanup. If that referencing record was also a graph-edge endpoint, its edges were then removed without consulting the edge table's `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` clause.

The result was a cross-table authorization bypass: a caller with delete permission on one table could erase edge records in another table, whose `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` denied them, by deleting an endpoint reached through a `REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE`.

### Impact

This affects deployments that combine `DEFINE FIELD ... REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE` with a referencing record that is also a graph-edge endpoint, where the edge table restricts deletion with a `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` clause.

What an attacker **can** do:

- With permission only to delete an endpoint vertex, cause the deletion of protected edge records on an edge table whose `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` clause denies them, when the deletion is routed through a `REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE`.
- Cause silent, unrecoverable loss of those edge records, which may carry business data.

What it **can't** do:

- Read the contents of the deleted edges - this is an integrity issue, not disclosure.
- Delete records on tables the caller cannot reach through such a cascade, or cross namespace or database isolation boundaries.
- Escalate to namespace- or root-level privileges. System users (root, namespace, database owners) are governed by their role, not by this flag, and are unaffected.

### Patches

The permission context is now split so the referential-integrity bypass no longer reaches the edge cascade. The reference `CASCADE` still disables permissions for the referencing record's own delete, but the record's edge cleanup runs under the caller's real permission state, so an edge table's `PERMISSIONS FOR delete` clause is evaluated exactly as it is for a direct `DELETE`. Edges the caller is not allowed to delete are left in place.

- Versions 3.3.0 and later are not affected by this issue.

### Workarounds

Users unable to patch should consider the following workarounds:

- Restrict vertex `DELETE` permission on tables that are reference-cascade targets to principals trusted to delete all connected edge records.
- Avoid `REFERENCE ON DELETE CASCADE` where the referencing record is also a graph-edge endpoint whose edge table relies on `PERMISSIONS FOR delete`.
- Use namespace or database isolation as the primary boundary where edge-level `PERMISSIONS` is load-bearing.

### References

- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE FIELD](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/field)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - Record references](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/datamodel/references)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - DEFINE TABLE … PERMISSIONS](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/define/table)
- [SurrealQL Documentation - RELATE statement](https://surrealdb.com/docs/surrealql/statements/relate)
- `fix(doc): keep the reference-CASCADE permission bypass out of the edge cascade` (included in SurrealDB 3.3.0)

### Acknowledgements

Thank you to [Yanhaoxi](https://github.com/Yanhaoxi) for reporting this issue.
